title: Oscar and the Orbit
premise: Coral Almeida has spent eleven years alone on Kepler Station, tending a terraforming garden for colonists who will never arrive and maintaining a beacon whose original commission records have been erased. When gravity stutters across the system for nine seconds, Coral discovers the beacon wasn't broadcasting to the living at all — it was answering something in dead space, an ancient relay that once held the minds of the system's first settlers. The flicker was a summons, and the jump window that lets her reach the relay closes in nineteen days. Racing there aboard a gutted survey skiff, Coral learns the relay's stored consciousnesses include the woman who commissioned her beacon — her mother, uploaded before Coral was born — and must choose between preserving the archive of the dead and sending one final message home, a choice that costs her the beacon but gives the unborn colonists a true inheritance.
about_author: Coral Sterling is the pen name of a former hydroponics engineer who spent six years on remote Antarctic research rotations before turning to fiction. She writes quiet, character-driven science fiction about people who keep things running when no one is watching.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: POV Coral. On an ordinary maintenance morning, gravity across the system stutters for exactly nine seconds; Coral floats through her greenhouse as forty years of careful planting drifts loose. She logs the anomaly, but station systems return nothing. Emotional beat: disorientation sharpening into dread — the first crack in a life built on routine.

chapters.title: The Garden for No One
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Surveying damage, Coral reflects on the colony ship that never came and the birth-cohort manifests she tends like graves. She finds one anomalous reading: during the flicker, her beacon transmitted outward despite being receive-only. Emotional beat: loneliness reframed as complicity — she has been part of something she never understood.

chapters.title: Records That Erase Themselves
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Digging into the beacon's commission file, Coral finds it scrubbed — not deleted, but actively rewritten every seventy-two hours by a process older than her assignment. A fragment survives: a name, M. Almeida. Emotional beat: vertigo of identity; the past is being maintained by someone, or something.

chapters.title: The Voice in the Buffer
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Replaying the nine-second transmission, Coral isolates a compressed signal beneath the carrier wave: structured, deliberate, repeating her own call sign back at her. Something in dead space knows she exists. Emotional beat: terror braided with a terrible, hungry hope of being known.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Coral calculates the orbital mechanics: a natural jump window opens toward the signal's origin in nineteen days and won't recur for a decade. She begins stripping the survey skiff Perihelion for the trip, arguing with herself that this is madness. Emotional beat: decision crystallizing — duty to the garden versus duty to the truth.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Was For
chapters.summary: POV Coral, with flashback interludes. Preparing for departure, Coral recalls her childhood on the inner stations and the mother who vanished on a relay crew when Coral was four. She realizes the commission date of her beacon is the week after her mother disappeared. Emotional beat: grief recontextualized; the mystery becomes personal.

chapters.title: Leaving the Light On
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Coral sets the greenhouse to autonomous mode, records messages for colonists who may never come, and launches. The station shrinks to a lit seed in the dark. Emotional beat: severance and resolve — leaving the only home she has, carrying its purpose with her.

chapters.title: Dead Space Rules
chapters.summary: POV Coral. In transit, Coral navigates the debris shoals of an abandoned shipping lane, salvaging fuel from a derelict hauler and meeting its feral maintenance drone, which imprints on her skiff. Emotional beat: grim resourcefulness; the emptiness of the system made vivid, and a first companion gained.

chapters.title: The Signal Learns Her Name
chapters.summary: POV Coral. The incoming transmission grows more complex, resolving into partial audio: a voice mid-sentence, cut off decades ago, saying a phrase Coral's mother used to sing. Coral answers openly for the first time. Emotional beat: intimacy with the impossible; hope becoming dangerous.

chapters.title: Interference
chapters.summary: POV Coral. A military patrol pings the Perihelion; Coral hides in a comet's tail while an officer's broadcast reveals the gravity flicker was detected system-wide and officially denied. Someone powerful wants the event buried. Emotional beat: paranoia closing in; she is now a witness nobody wants alive.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Fuel nearly spent, Coral reaches the coordinates: a cathedral-scale structure of black alloy drifting beyond the heliopause, still warm after two hundred years. The beacon's twin sits at its heart, transmitting inward. Emotional beat: awe and smallness before something vast and patient.

chapters.title: Doors That Remember Hands
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Boarding via EVA, Coral finds corridors that respond to her biometrics as if she were expected. Lights rise in sequences she somehow anticipates. The drone refuses to enter. Emotional beat: uncanny welcome — the relay has been waiting specifically for her.

chapters.title: The Archive of the Uploaded
chapters.summary: POV Coral. In the core, Coral discovers the truth: the relay holds the scanned minds of the first settlement generation, abandoned when funding collapsed, kept alive by solar trickle-charge and one loyal beacon. They have been calling for rescue, not contact. Emotional beat: horror and compassion entangled.

chapters.title: M. Almeida
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Among the archived minds, Coral finds her mother — younger than her memories, frozen mid-thought, aware only in fragments. Their first conversation spans minutes and years. Emotional beat: the reunion she never dared want, shadowed by everything it costs.

chapters.title: Why Gravity Flickered
chapters.summary: POV Coral. The archive explains: the relay's failing power drew on the system's gravitational reference network for nine seconds, risking collapse of all navigation. The flicker was a scream. If it happens again at full draw, ships everywhere fall out of the sky. Emotional beat: the personal mystery revealed as a ticking bomb.

chapters.title: The Choice of Currents
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Coral can reroute the relay's final reserves to send the archive's minds as a data ghost to the inner colonies — saving them but draining the beacon forever, or seal the archive safely dark and preserve the beacon for the unborn colonists' navigation. Either way, her mother's mind may not survive transfer. Emotional beat: love against duty made literal.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days, Spent
chapters.summary: POV Coral. The jump window begins closing; the patrol returns, demanding she abandon the site. Coral stalls them with the truth of the flicker, forcing the officer to choose between his orders and ten thousand endangered ships. Emotional beat: courage as persuasion; she stops hiding.

chapters.title: Transfer
chapters.summary: POV Coral. With the patrol standing down as reluctant witnesses, Coral initiates the transfer. Her mother's last coherent moments are spent telling Coral she chose the beacon's commission for her, so she would never be alone. Emotional beat: climax of grief and grace — being loved by design.

chapters.title: The Window Closes
chapters.summary: POV Coral. The data ghost launches through the closing jump window as the relay goes dark around her; Coral rides the collapsing gravity well back toward the inner system in a skiff with no margin. Emotional beat: white-knuckle release — everything risked, nothing certain.

chapters.title: What Comes Home
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Adrift and burning her last reserves, Coral is caught by the patrol vessel — the officer, changed by what he saw, grants her safe passage and files an honest report. The archive arrives at the colonial archives as the most complete record of the first generation ever recovered. Emotional beat: survival without triumph; consequences accepted.

chapters.title: A New Commission
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Months later, colonization is re-approved, partly because the archive proved the first generation's sacrifice and knowledge. Coral is asked to write the beacon's new commission record — in her own name, un-erasable. Emotional beat: belonging earned; the keeper becomes the founder.

chapters.title: Oscar and the Orbit
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Coral names the loyal salvage drone Oscar and plants the first seed of the next garden, the beacon relit above her with a new purpose: guiding the living instead of mourning the dead. Final line mirrors the opening — gravity steady, garden growing. Emotional beat: peace; memory transformed into inheritance.
